title: Retrospective intratumoral identification of bacterial species in oral squamous cell carcinoma and immunohistochemical and molecular biological characterization
summary: Despite modern therapeutic options, oral squamous cell carcinomas continue to exhibit high incidence and limited prognosis. Certain oral bacteria, particularly Porphyromonas gingivalis and various Fusobacterium species, may influence tumor development as well as the immune response within the tumor environment. The aim of this retrospective study is to investigate the impact of oral bacteria on the tumor microenvironment and immune response, in order to identify high-risk patients at an early stage and to enable targeted treatment decisions and the development of novel therapeutic approaches based on immunological and microbiological insights.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of the tongue, gingiva, base of tongue, and floor of the mouth (C01–C04)

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of 200 patients who underwent oncological resection of an oral squamous cell carcinoma between 2010 and 2023.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Voluntary consent and written signing of the informed consent form.

Surgical treatment in the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery at the University Medical Center Freiburg for an oral squamous cell carcinoma between 2010 and 2023, including deceased patients.

Tumor follow-up at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery with longitudinal data of at least 3 years.

Availability of archived tumor material that can be used for research purposes.
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal to participate in the study.

Patients with incomplete information on post-therapeutic follow-up.

Other tumor diseases or secondary malignancies.

Patients whose primary tumor was surgically treated at a different location.
